first_impression.reaction: Rhodes. We went there on a cruise years ago, all those old walls. The opening is sensible: four parts of the island, and it depends on guest numbers and the sort of ceremony. No gushing, no slang. I'll read it properly, top to bottom, with a cup of tea.

journey.quote: Greek summers bring frequent heatwaves and a wildfire season from June to September, so plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback for a summer date.
journey.reaction: Good, the heat and the fires are right up the top where I can see them. My mother doesn't cope with 30 degrees, so that matters more to me than the sunsets.

journey.section: Rhodes wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Setting | Ceremony options | Capacity |
journey.reaction: Nine venues on one table is handy, though I had to slide it sideways on the iPad and nearly every capacity box says 'Not published'. I'll look at it with my husband on the computer.

journey.section: How to compare Rhodes venues like for like
journey.quote: House rules that a venue does not publish, from capacity to minimum nights, are confirmed in writing by your Wedded Advisor before you commit
journey.reaction: In writing, before we commit, and a person whose job it is to check. That's the accountability I want when we're putting in this kind of money.

journey.quote: The wedding coordinator provides a schedule, a costing sheet with deadlines, an outline of costs and an itinerary, and meets the couple on arrival.
journey.reaction: Now that's what I like to read. A costing sheet with deadlines means nobody gets a surprise bill. This is the one I'd underline for my husband.

journey.quote: Additional guests can stay in the hotel's apartments and studios in the village, a 10-minute walk away.
journey.reaction: A 10-minute walk is nothing for the young ones, but what is that walk like for an 88-year-old with a walking frame? Nothing on the whole page tells me about steps, slopes or access at any of these places.

journey.quote: The package's legal section covers the civil registry service, the marriage file and certificate, translation of documents between English and Greek, and administration fees.
journey.reaction: Translation included. That eases my worry about papers in a language none of us read.

journey.quote: Because of its popularity, it needs to be booked as far in advance as possible, so lock the chapel before anything else if it is the setting you want.
journey.reaction: Practical advice, plainly said. That's the kind of thing you find out too late otherwise.

journey.section: Getting to Rhodes for your wedding
journey.quote: Guests with schedule changes are told to contact their airline or travel agent.
journey.reaction: That's fine for the young ones. But who meets my mother at the airport and drives her to the hotel? There's nothing about arranged transfers.

journey.section: Getting to Rhodes for your wedding
journey.quote: The Entry/Exit System registers fingerprints and a photo on arrival and may cause border delays, so leave a buffer before the first event.
journey.reaction: Useful. I wouldn't have known that and I'd hate the family stuck in a queue on the rehearsal night.

journey.quote: Heatwaves are frequent over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and many major tourist sites have little shade.
journey.reaction: Honest, and I appreciate it. It makes me lean towards May or late September for Mum's sake. It doesn't say anything about travel or medical insurance for older guests, which is the next thing I'd ask.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: The embassy does not provide legal advice, and the onus is on you to present documents in the correct form.
journey.reaction: 'The onus is on you' gives me a little fright. So is it my daughter doing all this, or does the Advisor or the venue help her? A couple of hotels mention a planner handling it, but I can't tell who does it if she books through you.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: Beaches from Kolimbia to Prasonisi and villages such as Embonas and Soroni are on the list too.
journey.reaction: By here the list of places had lost me. It's more detail than I need; I skimmed to the next heading.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: Read Smartraveller's Greece advice before you travel; its overall level for Greece is "Exercise normal safety precautions".
journey.reaction: I know Smartraveller. Pointing me to the government site is reassuring, not salesy.

journey.section: Shortlist your Rhodes venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, our time zone, AUD, and the fee in writing. That's the paragraph my husband needs to see. I'd still want a phone call before a cent changes hands.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues can a guest with a walking frame actually get around, from the room to the ceremony spot and the reception? Lindos especially.
Who arranges a private car from the airport for older guests?
What travel and medical insurance should older guests have, given the heat and fire warnings?
Who does the legal paperwork in practice if we book through Wedded Concierge: my daughter, the venue's planner or the Wedded Advisor?
Is the deposit protected, and who reads a contract written in Greek and in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Rhodes time?
Is the first step a phone call with a real person, before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the closing section (fee in writing, AUD, one person) and the Melenos costing sheet line
My daughter, with the heat and wildfire advice and the note to book St Paul's Chapel early
My sister, who will look after Mum on the trip, with the airport border delay and heat advice

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: A named person, our time zone, AUD and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if I knew a real person rings me first, and that they'd check which of these places my mother can get around.

top_3_changes: Mention access for older or less mobile guests at least once (for example a line in the comparison section asking each venue about steps and step-free routes, and adding it to what the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing). At the moment the page never raises it.

Next to the heat and wildfire advice, add one plain line telling families to arrange travel and medical insurance that suits older guests, and mention organised airport transfers in the getting-there section.

After 'the onus is on you', add one plain sentence on who does the legal paperwork in practice (the couple, with the Advisor's or venue planner's help), and shorten the long list of civil ceremony places in the 'Where' paragraph.

open_questions.question: Unlike Santorini, the Rhodes draft never mentions mobility, steps or accessibility for older guests, which is this persona's top practical worry. Treat as should-fix? Insurance, organised transfers and who handles legal paperwork are smaller gaps. Deposit protection, contract language and on-the-day contact are deferred business details.
